questions.q: What does a one-to-many relationship mean?
options: Many rows on each side can reference many rows on the other
Both tables must have the exact same number of rows
The relationship only works with composite primary keys
One row on the 'one' side can be referenced by many rows on the 'many' side, but each 'many' row points back to exactly one 'one' row
questions.explain: That asymmetry — many pointing to one — is the definition of one-to-many.

questions.q: What extra trick is needed to make a foreign key relationship one-to-many, compared to one-to-one?
options: The foreign key column must also be a primary key
A CHECK constraint must explicitly allow duplicates
You must create a linking table in between
None — it's just an ordinary foreign key with no UNIQUE constraint restricting it
questions.explain: One-to-many is the default shape of a plain foreign key; one-to-one requires the extra step of also making it unique.

questions.q: In AdventureWorks2012, what is the real one-to-many example between SalesOrderHeader and SalesOrderDetail?
options: Every order must have exactly one line item
One line item has many orders
One order (SalesOrderHeader row) has many line items (SalesOrderDetail rows), each pointing back to that one order
SalesOrderHeader and SalesOrderDetail have no relationship
questions.explain: SalesOrderDetail.SalesOrderID is a foreign key to SalesOrderHeader, and it's not unique on its own — many detail rows can share one order.

questions.q: Why can multiple SalesOrderDetail rows share the same SalesOrderID?
options: Because SalesOrderID alone isn't the primary key — the real primary key is the composite of SalesOrderID and SalesOrderDetailID together
Because SalesOrderID is nullable
Because SalesOrderDetail has no primary key at all
Because SalesOrderHeader allows duplicate SalesOrderIDs
questions.explain: Since SalesOrderID by itself isn't constrained to be unique in SalesOrderDetail, many rows can carry the same value.

questions.q: When designing a new schema, how do you get a one-to-many relationship 'for free'?
options: Add a UNIQUE constraint to the foreign key column
Add a plain foreign key with no additional UNIQUE constraint on it
Make the foreign key column the primary key of the same table
One-to-many cannot be created intentionally — it only happens by accident
questions.explain: Every ordinary, unconstrained foreign key defaults to one-to-many unless you deliberately restrict it to be unique.
